result:
12 rules in `pricebook.py` didn't match their docstrings (or the module docstring's general rules), and I fixed all of them. I then checked every rule (1–150) against what its docstring says, across many quantities and unit prices, and all now match.

| Rule | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 03, 138 | The cap was applied to the price the discount is computed from, not to the discount | Compute the discount first, then cap it |
| 41 | Same problem: the cap was applied to `base` | Compute the discount first, then cap it |
| 09 | `qty > 12`, so exactly 12 units got no discount | Changed to `qty >= 12` |
| 24 | The threshold was 21 | Changed to 20 |
| 19 | Marked "marginal" but discounted every unit | Discount only the units above the threshold |
| 112 | Marked "whole" but discounted only the units above the threshold | Discount every unit (`base`) |
| 50, 61, 96, 128 | The cap only applied once the discount passed twice the cap | The cap now always applies |
| 142 | Used `round()` instead of rounding down to the won | Changed to `// 100` |

STATUS: DONE
